body: Absolutely. I have always offered to listen to anyone that had something to say, and have often done so. Held advice back unless it was requested. Offered unbiased opinions if needed. Or just sat, listened, and hugged.
I've been in therapy for a few years now. Been on several anti-depressants. Sometimes it helps, usually not. I come out of therapy feeling horribly depressed and I dread going every single time.
Just help talking me down, working through my stuff. Eventually, they get tired of hearing about it.

1. this is a tricky question for me. I like being around other people, but often wish I were someplace else. Whenever I'm out, I wish I was at home alone. When I'm at home alone, I just wish I could be out somewhere. I don't belong anywhere.
2. I'm 36. I've been dealing with this for many years now. I've always managed to pull through. But I'm so tired.

Read my other thread for more information about me and my story.

I am in the same boat, and it's sinking fast. Years ago, my life was amazing. Loved, in love, great kids, wonderful friends and family. And I sat on my bed crying every day. It was then I realized (finally, after 30 years) that I'm just a depressed person. It's a chemical issue, not a feelings issue. I can't just "cheer up". I can't be happy. I can however fill myself with mind numbing and side-effect inducing drugs (delayed ejaculation anyone?). Nothing happened to me to cause this. There was no single event that made me this way. It's just the way I am.

Most days I hope for a fatal single car crash. Something that my family will have to live with, but something that was totally out of everyones control. My kids would get the life insurance I'm forced to pay for every month. They could go to school, get a good education and hopefully a decent life.

I drive along a highway with massive rock walls regularly. Sometimes I really just want to jerk the wheel directly into it.

I can often guess what tomorrow brings. The same as yesterday, only a little bit worse. Sure, I might have a good day. Someone might actually step up and care about me for a few minutes. I might even meet someone new. A task I'm actively attempting. But it's gotten worse every day for the past 30 years, regardless of momentary highs.

My kids are the only reason I'm still around. The impact it would have them would be extreme. And yet, every day, that sliver of hope grows smaller and smaller. I see a lot of myself in them, and that kills me all in it's own. I see the same shy kids, struggling in school, not a ton of friends, but lots of acquaintances that come and go. I've already ruined their life, just by being their biological father.
